zh.title: 阿聯酋航空工程署推出「材料未來工作室」大學生計畫
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空工程署於2026年7月30日啟動「材料未來工作室」六週課程，挑戰大學生重新構想退役航空材料並轉化為新產品。該計畫由「循環利用」部門領導，將學生與航空專業人士合作，解決實際的產業挑戰。
body: 阿聯酋航空工程署於2026年7月30日推出「材料未來工作室」計畫，為大學生設計六週課程，挑戰他們重新構想退役航空材料並轉化為新產品。該計畫由阿聯酋航空工程署內的「循環利用」部門領導，將學生與航空專業人士配對，共同解決實際的產業挑戰。
首次課程共聚攜23名來自卡拉菲大學、阿聯酋航空大學及沙哈大學的學生。計畫於啟動之初舉辦導向性課程與參觀阿聯酋航空工程署設施，讓學生與高階主管會面，並 firsthand了解維修作業，包括對阿聯酋航空機隊進行的A檢與C檢，以及循環利用工廠。
學生將在六週內應用所學，發展航空材料循環利用與再利用的新概念。整個構想與概念發展階段中，他們會密切與阿聯酋航空工程署團隊成員合作，獲得指導。
計畫將於結束時舉辦最終展示，讓學生呈現他們的構想與原型，展示如何將循環利用的材料轉化為創新產品。透過結合學術研究與實務產業曝光，該計畫旨在為學生提供實際技能，並加深對航空工程生態系統的理解。
此計畫連結阿聯酋航空的廣泛改造計畫，該計畫投資數十億美元，旨在對219架空中巴士A380及波音777號機進行全面翻新，以提升客戶體驗。作為該項目的一部分，從翻新的航空器中移除的材料正被循環利用，由阿聯酋航空工程署在迪拜的專屬團隊領導，將退役航空材料轉化為手工製成的產品，以減少廢棄物。
該計畫建構在阿聯酋航空既有的其他循環利用計畫基礎上，包括「Aircrafted by Emirates」收藏系列，該系列製成限量版行李箱、袋子及配件，均使用回收的航空內飾材料。計畫亦補充了「Aircrafted KIDS」計畫，將在改造計畫中復原的布料及其他材料轉化為手工背包，目的是為兒童捐贈。迄今為止，該努力已捐贈超過4,000個背包到11個國家的兒童。

en.title: Emirates Engineering launches Material Futures Studio for university students
en.summary: Emirates Engineering launched a six-week Material Futures Studio program on July 30, challenging university students to reimagine retired aircraft materials and collaborate with aviation professionals to solve real-world challenges.
body: Emirates Engineering launched the Material Futures Studio program on July 30, 2026, offering a six-week course that challenges university students to reimagine retired aircraft materials and transform them into new products. The initiative is led by the Upcycling department within Emirates Engineering, pairing students with aviation professionals to tackle real-world industry challenges.

The first edition brought together 23 students from Khalifa University, Emirates Aviation University, and the University of Sharjah. The program opened with an orientation and tour of Emirates Engineering facilities, where students met with senior leaders and got a firsthand look at maintenance operations, including A-checks and C-checks performed on the Emirates fleet, along with the upcycling shop where materials are currently being repurposed.

Over the course of six weeks, students apply what they learned during orientation to develop new concepts for upcycling and reusing aircraft materials into original products. Throughout the ideation and concept development stages, they work closely with members of the Emirates Engineering team for guidance.

The program will wrap up with a final showcase where students present their concepts and prototypes for upcycled materials. By combining academic study with hands-on industry exposure, the initiative is designed to give students practical skills and a deeper understanding of the aviation engineering ecosystem, while giving Emirates a chance to engage with young talent and surface new ideas in the process.

Material Futures Studio connects to a broader retrofit program at Emirates, a multi-billion-dollar investment to fully refurbish 219 Airbus A380 and Boeing 777 aircraft aimed at improving the customer experience across its fleet. As part of that project, materials removed from retrofitted aircraft are being repurposed through upcycling work led entirely in-house by Emirates Engineering in Dubai, with a dedicated team turning retired aircraft materials into handcrafted products meant to cut down on waste.

The new student program builds on other upcycling initiatives already underway at the airline, including the Aircrafted by Emirates collection, a line of limited-edition luggage, bags, and accessories made from reclaimed aircraft interiors. It also complements the Aircrafted KIDS initiative, which turns fabrics and other materials recovered during the retrofit program into handmade backpacks for children. To date, that effort has resulted in more than 4,000 backpacks donated to children across 11 countries.
